items.description: Analyze repository structure and initialize project skeleton
items.acceptance_criteria: Create repo_analysis.md documenting all existing modules (.archivara/semantic_scholar.py, .archivara/concept_evolve.py), their APIs, and how the researcher should use them. Create a project directory structure with at least: src/, tests/, results/, and a requirements.txt listing numpy as a dependency.

items.description: Literature review of classical N-body gravitational simulation methods
items.acceptance_criteria: Use web search to find and summarize at least 5 foundational references covering: Newton's law of universal gravitation for point masses, the direct-summation O(N^2) approach, softened gravitational potentials, and the distinction between collisional vs collisionless N-body methods. Document findings in literature_review.md with inline citations.

items.description: Literature review of numerical integration schemes for Hamiltonian systems
items.acceptance_criteria: Use web search and Semantic Scholar to find and summarize at least 5 references on symplectic integrators: forward Euler, Stoermer-Verlet (leapfrog), Yoshida 4th-order, and Ruth 3rd-order methods. Document time-reversibility, symplectic properties, and order of convergence for each. Append findings to literature_review.md.

items.description: Survey hierarchical force-computation algorithms and open-source simulators
items.acceptance_criteria: Use web search to review the Barnes-Hut tree algorithm (O(N log N)) and at least 2 open-source N-body codes (e.g., REBOUND, Gadget, NBODY6). Document the multipole acceptance criterion (theta parameter), quadrupole corrections, and trade-offs. Append to literature_review.md.

items.description: Create and populate sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted sources
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib exists in the repo root with valid BibTeX entries for at least 10 relevant papers and resources. Must include entries for: Barnes & Hut 1986, Verlet 1967, Yoshida 1990, Aarseth 2003 (or equivalent foundational works), plus at least 6 additional relevant references. Each entry has author, title, year, and journal/venue fields.

items.description: Run ConceptEvolve to discover cross-domain insights for gravity simulation
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve.py evolve with the gravity simulation research problem. Save outputs to results/concept_evolve/. Document at least 3 actionable steering directions in literature_review.md that connect gravity simulation to other domains (e.g., electrostatics, molecular dynamics, swarm behavior).

items.description: Implement Body and System data structures
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/body.py with a Body class (mass, position as 2D numpy array, velocity as 2D numpy array) and a System class that holds a list of Bodies and provides vectorized position/velocity/mass accessors as numpy arrays. At least 3 unit tests in tests/test_body.py pass.

items.description: Implement brute-force O(N^2) gravitational force computation
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/forces.py with a brute_force_gravity(system) function that computes pairwise gravitational accelerations using vectorized numpy operations with a softening parameter epsilon. Verify correctness: for a two-body system with known masses and separation, computed force matches F = G*m1*m2/r^2 to within 1% (accounting for softening). At least 3 unit tests pass.

items.description: Implement symplectic Euler and leapfrog (Stoermer-Verlet) integrators
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/integrators.py with euler_step(system, dt, force_fn) and leapfrog_step(system, dt, force_fn) functions. Both modify positions and velocities in-place. Leapfrog must use the kick-drift-kick or drift-kick-drift form. At least 4 unit tests pass, including a test that a circular two-body orbit remains stable for 100 orbits with leapfrog (energy drift < 0.1%).

items.description: Implement energy and momentum conservation metrics
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/metrics.py with functions: total_kinetic_energy(system), total_potential_energy(system, G, epsilon), total_energy(system, G, epsilon), total_momentum(system), and total_angular_momentum(system). All return scalar or vector values. At least 4 unit tests pass, including verification that kinetic + potential = total energy for a known configuration.

items.description: Run baseline brute-force benchmarks and establish reference performance
items.acceptance_criteria: Create benchmarks/baseline_bench.py that measures wall-clock time for brute-force force computation at N = 10, 50, 100, 500, 1000 particles (5 trials each). Record results to results/baseline_benchmarks.json. Verify O(N^2) scaling by fitting log(time) vs log(N) and confirming slope is between 1.8 and 2.2. Generate a log-log scaling plot saved as results/scaling_baseline.png.

items.description: Implement Barnes-Hut quadtree for hierarchical force computation
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/barnes_hut.py with a QuadTree class supporting: insert(body), compute_center_of_mass(), and compute_acceleration(body, theta) using the multipole acceptance criterion. Theta parameter must be configurable (default 0.5). At least 5 unit tests pass, including: (a) tree correctly partitions 100 random bodies, (b) force on a single body matches brute-force within 5% for theta=0.3, (c) empty quadrant handling works.

items.description: Implement Yoshida 4th-order symplectic integrator
items.acceptance_criteria: Add yoshida4_step(system, dt, force_fn) to src/integrators.py using Yoshida's 4th-order coefficients (w0, w1). Verify 4th-order convergence: run a Kepler orbit with dt and dt/2, confirm error ratio is approximately 16 (2^4). At least 3 unit tests pass, including convergence order verification.

items.description: Implement adaptive timestep control
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/adaptive.py with an adaptive_step(system, dt_initial, force_fn, integrator, tolerance) function that adjusts dt based on acceleration magnitudes or energy conservation error. Must halve dt when close encounters occur (minimum separation < threshold) and restore it when bodies are well-separated. At least 3 unit tests pass, including a test with a highly eccentric orbit where dt is visibly reduced at periapsis.

items.description: Implement initial condition generators and canonical test problems
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/initial_conditions.py with functions: circular_binary(m1, m2, a), figure_eight_3body(), plummer_sphere(N, M, a), and random_uniform(N, box_size, max_vel). Each returns a System object. Verify circular binary period matches Kepler's third law to within 1%. At least 4 unit tests pass.

items.description: Implement visualization module for trajectories and energy diagnostics
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/visualization.py with functions: plot_trajectories(history, filename), plot_energy(time_series, energy_series, filename), and plot_snapshot(system, filename). All save matplotlib figures to specified paths. Generate at least one sample plot from a 3-body figure-eight run saved to results/sample_trajectory.png.

items.description: Benchmark Barnes-Hut vs brute-force scaling
items.acceptance_criteria: Run both force computation methods at N = 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000 (3 trials each). Record wall-clock times to results/bh_vs_bf_benchmarks.json. Generate a log-log comparison plot (results/bh_vs_bf_scaling.png). Barnes-Hut must be faster than brute-force for N >= 500. Fit scaling exponents for both methods.

items.description: Compare integrator accuracy on Kepler orbit benchmark
items.acceptance_criteria: Run a Kepler orbit (e=0.5) for 100 orbital periods using Euler, leapfrog, and Yoshida4, each at dt = T/100, T/200, T/500 where T is the orbital period. Measure: (a) relative energy error at end, (b) maximum energy error, (c) orbital precession. Save results to results/integrator_comparison.json and generate a convergence plot (results/integrator_convergence.png) showing error vs dt on log-log axes.

items.description: Theta parameter sweep for Barnes-Hut accuracy vs speed trade-off
items.acceptance_criteria: Run Barnes-Hut force computation on a 1000-body Plummer sphere with theta = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.5. For each theta, measure: (a) RMS force error relative to brute-force, (b) wall-clock time. Save results to results/theta_sweep.json. Generate a two-panel plot (results/theta_sweep.png) showing error vs theta and speedup vs theta. Identify the Pareto-optimal theta value.

items.description: Run canonical test problems and validate against known solutions
items.acceptance_criteria: Simulate: (a) circular binary for 1000 orbits — verify energy conservation < 1e-6 with leapfrog, (b) figure-eight 3-body for 50 periods — verify periodic return to within 1% of initial positions, (c) Plummer sphere with N=500 for 10 crossing times — verify virial ratio stays within 0.9-1.1. Save trajectory plots and diagnostics to results/. Document all results in results/canonical_tests.md.

items.description: Convergence study: energy conservation as a function of timestep
items.acceptance_criteria: For leapfrog and Yoshida4 integrators, run a 10-body random system for 100 time units at dt = 0.1, 0.05, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.001. Plot maximum relative energy error vs dt on log-log axes. Confirm leapfrog shows 2nd-order convergence (slope ~2) and Yoshida4 shows 4th-order (slope ~4). Save plot to results/convergence_study.png and data to results/convergence_study.json.

items.description: Write comprehensive research report
items.acceptance_criteria: Create REPORT.md (at least 1500 words) with sections: Introduction, Methods (force computation, integration schemes, Barnes-Hut), Results (benchmarks, accuracy, canonical tests), Discussion (comparing against prior work cited in sources.bib), and Conclusion. Include at least 5 inline figure references and 8 citations to sources.bib entries.

items.description: Create summary comparison tables against prior work
items.acceptance_criteria: Add a section to REPORT.md with at least 2 tables: (a) integrator comparison table (method, order, energy error at dt=0.01, wall-clock time) with a column noting published values from the literature, (b) Barnes-Hut performance table (theta, error, speedup) compared against published benchmarks from referenced papers. All table entries must cite their source.

items.description: Document limitations, open questions, and future directions
items.acceptance_criteria: Create LIMITATIONS.md listing: at least 3 known limitations of the implementation (e.g., 2D only, no parallelism, no periodic boundaries), at least 3 open research questions, and at least 3 concrete future directions (e.g., extend to 3D, add FMM, GPU acceleration). Each item must be 2-3 sentences with references to relevant literature.

items.description: Create reproducibility package with README, requirements.txt, and run_all.py
items.acceptance_criteria: Update README.md with: project description, installation instructions, usage examples for running simulations, and description of all output files. Create run_all.py that executes all benchmarks and generates all plots. Verify that 'python run_all.py' completes without errors and produces all expected output files in results/. Validate sources.bib has at least 10 entries with no malformed BibTeX.
